Pape, A., Severson-Baker, C., Woloshyniuk, G. and Jamin, Y. (2000). Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Opportunities for the Upstream Oil and Gas Sector and the Gas Pipeline Sectors in British Columbia. The Pembina Institute, July 2000, prepared for the David Suzuki Foundation.

Region: British Columbia and Canada (equipment-leak efficiencies originate in Alberta/US EPA studies). Locators are PRINTED page numbers (footer "Pembina Institute, July 2000  N"). The report is a qualitative survey with company case studies; it prints NO capital or operating costs per technology and no per-unit energy figures. Main file: leak control efficiencies by component and measure (Table 7, 13 rows), the gas boot storage-loss factor and its 86% reduction, the pig-valve 85-100% reduction, and three flare-gas power examples (30 kW and 75 kW microturbines, 2 MW gas turbine). Dollar examples (Shell, Talisman, SaskEnergy, CAODC) are in _measures; company-reported CO2E reductions and the B.C. 1995 emission inventory (Table 5) are in _other-values; Appendices B-E (initiative lists, codes ee-e, em-f etc.) are not extracted. Prices are CAD assumed with PRICE YEAR NOT STATED; publication year 2000 used. Control efficiencies are printed as fractions and stored as percent.
